density.label: Density
density.question: How much information must fit on one screen, and how often is it scanned?

compact.summary: Tight rhythm for scanning and comparing many items at once.
fitsWhen: data tables and dashboards used daily
expert users who scan, not read
tools where switching screens is costly

balanced.summary: Comfortable reading and doing; the default for most products.

airy.summary: Generous space that slows the reader down and gives each element weight.
fitsWhen: portfolios and brand pages with few items
avoid: padding so large that the first screen shows no content

temperature.label: Temperature
temperature.question: Should the interface feel warm and human, or cool and precise?

warm.summary: Neutrals tinted toward red-yellow; feels human, hospitable, handmade.

neutral.summary: Near-gray neutrals that let content and one accent carry the color.
fitsWhen: products whose brand color must dominate

cool.summary: Neutrals tinted toward blue-green; feels precise, technical, calm.
fitsWhen: products that must read as exact

formality.label: Formality
formality.question: How serious is the context: play, everyday use, or high stakes?

playful.summary: Loose rules, bigger contrasts in size, room for surprise.
avoid: playfulness in error, payment, or legal flows

approachable.summary: Friendly but orderly; plain language and clear structure.

formal.summary: Restrained, consistent, conservative; trust through order.

tokens.caseStyle: sentence case; no all-caps body text

motion.label: Motion energy
motion.question: What should motion do here: nothing, explain changes, or create an experience?

still.summary: State changes are instant or near-instant; motion only for feedback.

subtle.summary: Motion explains where things come from and go; never decorates.

expressive.summary: Motion is part of the identity: choreography, scroll-linked scenes, playful physics.

tokens.easing: custom curves or springs, defined as tokens

avoid: autoplay or parallax without a prefers-reduced-motion path

shape.label: Shape language
shape.question: Should edges read as exact and structural, or soft and friendly?

sharp.summary: Square or nearly square corners; structure comes from alignment and lines.
fitsWhen: dense grids where radii waste space

mixed.summary: Small radii on controls, near-square containers; reads as precise but not cold.
fitsWhen: products that pair data with friendly flows

soft.summary: Generous radii and rounded forms; reads as friendly and tactile.
avoid: the same large radius plus shadow on every element (vis/default-stack)

contrast.label: Contrast
contrast.question: How much visual drama between elements: quiet and even, or bold and stark?

low.summary: Quiet surfaces and close tones; hierarchy from type and space. Text still meets WCAG AA.

medium.summary: Clear separation of layers with restrained depth.

tokens.shadowPolicy: subtle shadows for overlays only; borders for structure

high.summary: Stark value contrast, heavy weights, big scale jumps; confident and loud.

tokens.shadowPolicy: hard edges or none; contrast from color blocks

voice.label: Typographic voice
voice.question: What should the letterforms say before anyone reads the words?

neutral-sans.summary: Invisible type that gets out of the way.
fitsWhen: products where the content is the brand

fontCategories: system UI stack or neo-grotesque sans

humanist.summary: Open, calligraphic sans; warm and readable at small sizes.

geometric.summary: Circles and straight lines; modern, constructed, optimistic.
fitsWhen: product launches, design tools, modern brands

editorial-serif.summary: Serif headings or text; authority, literacy, considered pace.

technical-mono.summary: Monospace accents; precise, engineered, honest about being a tool.

display.summary: A distinctive display face carries identity; body stays plain.
fitsWhen: portfolios with a strong point of view

fontCategories: plain sans or serif for body

avoid: more than two families plus mono

imagery.label: Imagery
imagery.question: Does the product sell through pictures, through words, or both?

type-led.summary: Typography, layout, and real data carry the page; images are rare and purposeful.
avoid: stock illustrations used to fill space

balanced.summary: Real product views or photos support the words.
fitsWhen: SaaS marketing with a visual product

imagery-led.summary: Photography, product shots, or 3D lead; type frames them.
avoid: text over images without a contrast-safe scrim
unoptimized hero images that delay LCP

conflicts.message: Expressive motion on a compact, high-frequency surface slows repeated tasks; confine it to onboarding or marketing pages.
Airy, type-led, and low contrast together often read as empty; add a signature move or raise contrast.
Display faces undercut formality; limit them to a wordmark or a single page-level heading.
Soft shapes with stark contrast can look toy-like; check the swap test against the audience.
Playful tone on a cool, compact surface sends mixed signals; decide which one the audience needs.
